items.stem: A sign gives students 10 percent off and orders over 1,000 pesos 5 percent off. A student buys 1,200 pesos of books. Two cashiers charge 1,080 and 1,020 pesos. What caused the gap?

options.text: One of the cashiers cannot do basic arithmetic.
options.feedback: Each amount follows from a rule: 10 percent off gives 1,080 and 15 percent off gives 1,020. The arithmetic is fine.

options.text: The sign never said what happens when both rules apply.
options.feedback: The table has a row for a student with a large order, and the sign left it blank, so each cashier chose an answer.

options.text: Students should never get the large-order discount.
options.feedback: The sign did not say so, so each cashier made a guess.

items.stem: A rule says "orders over 1,000 pesos get 5 percent off." A customer pays exactly 1,000 pesos and gets no discount. The customer is upset. What is the best fix?

options.text: Write the edge in the rule: "1,000 pesos or more."
options.feedback: Stating the edge in words, and testing it, removes the argument at the counter.

options.text: Tell the customer that the sign was clear.
options.feedback: The sign said "over," and the customer expected "at least." The store has to choose one on purpose.

options.text: Remove the rule so that nobody gets a discount.
options.feedback: Removing the rule loses a discount that works for most orders.

items.stem: A decision table has two yes or no conditions. A third condition, member or not, is added. How many rows does the table need?

options.text: Six rows, since each new condition adds two rows.
options.feedback: Each new condition doubles the rows, so adding two would leave combinations out.

options.text: Three rows, one for each condition.
options.feedback: A row exists for every combination of conditions, so three conditions need more than three rows.

options.text: Eight rows, since each new condition doubles the count.

items.stem: A developer writes the check for "the first 50 members get a gift" as member number less than 50. The 50th member gets no gift. Which test would have caught it?

options.feedback: A value far from the edge gives the same answer under both versions of the rule.
A value below, at and above the edge shows which side each value falls on.
A value far above the edge also gives the same answer under both versions.
